- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or sentiment reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward by 2–5% in next period.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; if true outcome shows strong upward trend in last 5–7 days, increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is flat or declining, model overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–2% to reflect sentiment mismatch.
- When sentiment is negative but price is rising, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to capture sentiment reversal or momentum.
